sentences.text: Finding Curvorudentis in Late Jurassic rocks of Germany pushes its known range to the youngest Jurassic deposits.
Fossils of the genus have been recorded from four separate localities.
The original description relied on a single complete tooth and two highly fragmentary teeth, indicating a dentition adapted for grasping prey.
Curvorudentis is a valid genus placed within the class Chondrichthyes, the cartilaginous fishes.
It belongs to the subclass Galeomorphii, although its precise affinities within that group are uncertain.
The type species, originally described as Synechodus prorogatus by Kriwet in 2003, now serves as the reference for the genus.
Current interpretations view Curvorudentis prorogatus as a galeomorph shark rather than a member of the stem clade Synechodontiformes.
The genus lived from the Callovian to the Kimmeridgian ages of the Middle to Late Jurassic, roughly 165.3 to 152.21 million years ago.
Its fossils have been recovered in what is now Germany and Poland.
Researchers still disagree about the exact systematic placement of Curvorudentis within Galeomorphii.
